SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. B. REGISTRY
File No. D-6479
Section 3, Special Branch.
REPORT
Date. April 11, 1938.
Subject The Comintern and the United Front Campaign.
Made by D.I. Sun Pao-hwa Forwarded by R.B. Laversit.

Reference to the information recently received
to the effect that the Comintern has issued instructions to
the following communist organizations to accelerate the
United Front Campaign movement:
a) Workers International Relief.
b) League against Imperialism and for National
Independence.
c) Friends of the Soviet Union.
d) World Committee against War and Fascism.
e) International Class War Prisoners' Aid.
f) Society for Cultural Relations with Soviet
Russia.
g) International Union of the Revolutionary
Theatre.
h) International Juridicial Association.
Of these eight organizations only the first four
are known to have definitely functioned in Shanghai, and at
the present time even they are more or less dormant. There
is little doubt that the arrest during the first six months
of 1931 of Koo Cheng Chang (顧順章), Chief of the Special
Administrative Bureau of the Chinese Communist Party, of
Paul Noulens, Secretary of the Pan Pacific Trade Union
Secretariat, and of Hsian; Tsoong Fuh (向忠發), Secretary-
General of the C.C.P., created an unprecedented disruption
of the activities of the C.C.P. Police raids which also
caused consternation of the Party were carried out during
the next two years on the local headquarters of the Communist
Youth League, Kiangsu Provincial Committee, Military Committee
and the National Labour Federation. As these setbacks

constituted vital injuries to the Party, "Central" members
either proceeded to outports or Red districts, while others
remained in hiding in Shanghai. An illustration of the
commotion existing at this time was evident in the flight
from Shanghai to Soviet areas of Chen Shao Yue (陈绍禹)
and Zing Paung Chien (秦邦宪), Secretary-General and acting
Secretary-General of the C.C.P. respectively.
Sometime in 1933, the Party resolved to adopt
an offensive campaign in all its branches and organized
various "mass" bodies such as the Anti-Imperialist, Anti-
Japanese, Anti-War, and Anti-Fascist organizations, etc.
About this time Communist Central elected a
new administrative officials and an executive committee
of 175 members. Party headquarters were transferred to
Soviet areas and China Proper was divided into three areas:-
North, East and South, with each division under the control
of a Central delegate known as the Secretary-General.
In 1934, an organization entitled the "People's
Armed Self-Defence Committee" was formed. Despite the
fact that these "mass" organizations were organized in the
first instance by persons not connected with the Party, they
eventually came under the control of a "communist nucleus."
On the instructions of Party headquarters, all such "mass"
bodies commenced to work in co-operation and constituted
what is known as the "United Front Campaign."
Following the arrest of Yue Kyi Zien (乐琪全)
alias Lee Tsok Sung (李竹声), who succeeded Chen Shao Yue
as Secretary-General of the Party in 1933, by the Settlement
Police at No.38 Race Course Road on June 26, 1934, a lack

of a stimulating force was felt by the aforementioned bodies
and coupled with the veiled threats administered by the Blue
Shirts to Madame Sun Yat Sen and other prominent leaders,
these institutions gradually became dormant.
The arrest of Hoyang Chi Siu (歐陽赤秀) (reported
to have been apprehended by the Shanghai Bureau of Public
Safety in Chinese controlled territory on 19.2.35), of Tien
Han (田漢), arrested under the name of Tung Tsh Seng (陳哲生)
by the Shanghai Municipal Police on 20.2.35 in house No.11,
Oen Zung Li (安宗理), Shanhaikwan Road, and of Chu Tse Ming
(朱則明) alias Tsz Ching Ngoo (朱鏡吾), reported to be Secretary-
General of the Eastern Bureau of the C.C.P. completed the
wreckage of the United Front Campaign.
The present location of Central Soviet Headquarters
in Southern Szechuen prevents easy intercommunication between
Communist Central and Shanghai, and, coupled with the lack of
adequately trained personnel to assume executive positions
caused by the arrest of prominent members, presents an
obstacle which the Party must overcome before renewing
its activities on an extended scale.
Kuh Tao-hua
D. I.
D.C. (Special Branch)

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
Section 2, Special Branch
REPORT
File No. 6479
Date 10, 1935.
Subject Organizations associated with the "United Front Campaign."
Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa Forwarded by [Signature] 89

I respectfully wish to state that the mention of
April, 1932, in the third paragraph of my report dated
March 15, 1935, as being the occasion on which the Chinese
Communist Party suffered severe reverses is incorrect.
A typing error in the previous report was unfortunately
overlooked.

There is little doubt that the arrest during the
first six months of 1931 of Koo Cheng Chang (顾顺章), Chief
of the Special Administrative Bureau of the Chinese Communist
Party, of Paul Noulens, Secretary of the Pan Pacific Trade
Union Secretariat, and of Hsiang Tsoong Fah (向忠发),
Secretary-General of the C.C.P., created an unprecedented
disruption of the activities of the C.C.P.

The mention in the Straits Settlement Police Journal
of the existence in Shanghai of a "Red" Central is correct
only up to February 19, 1935. On this date Chu Tse Ming
(朱则明) alias Tsz Ching Ngoo (朱镜吾), reported to be
Secretary-General of the C.C.P., was arrested by the French
Police on information given by the Chinese authorities. He
was subsequently extradited to the Public Safety Bureau.

It is learned from a reliable source that Chu was the successor
of the former Secretary-General Yue Kyi Zien (余吉全), who
was arrested by the Settlement Police at No.38 Race Course
Road on 26.6.34 and extradited to the Shanghai Bureau of
Public Safety on 4.7.34 (vide File D-5968).

Kuh Pao-hwa
S2. D. I.
Please prepare a report with
all inaccuracies corrected
which will contain all the
information required in forming
a reply to the Deputy C. of M.
10 APR 1935
D.C. (Special Branch)

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch.
REPORT
File No. S. B. REGISTER
D
Date March 15, 1935.

Subject Organizations associated with the 'United Front Campaign'.

Made by D.I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [签名]

In compliance with the instructions of the D. C.
Special Branch of March 5, 1935, I have to state that certain
of the Komintern organs mentioned in the attached report were
functioning in 1933 in Shanghai. This was borne out in fact
by the convention at No. 34 Paoting Road on September 30, 1933,
of the Anti-War Congress which was headed by Lord Marley and
his foreign entourage and which was held under the auspices of
the World Committee against War and Fascism.

Apart from a remote possibility of the existence in
China of the International Judicial Association, the remaining
organizations mentioned in the communique from the British
Consulate-General claim to function not only in various parts
of China but in all large cities throughout the world. Among
active members of such organizations in China can be cited
Madame Sun Yat Sen née Soong Ching Ling, Aoyang Chi Sieu (歐陽繼修)
(alleged to have been arrested by the Shanghai Bureau of Public
Safety in Chinese controlled territory on 19.2.35) and Dien Han
(田漢) arrested under the name of Zung Tsh Seng (陳哲生)
by the Shanghai Municipal Police on 20.2.35 in house No. 11 Oen
Zung Li (安遠里), Shanhaikwan Road.

Since April 1932 the local organs of the Chinese
Communist Party have sustained serious reverses from the hands
of the local Chinese, French and Settlement Authorities,
following a series of raids on certain of the administrative
offices of the Party and its auxiliary organizations; it follows
therefore that the Party's scattered forces have been unable
to resuscitate themselves so as to function as an active body.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

D. C. (Special Branch).
18 MAR. 1935

（左侧手写批注）：
$2,
Why should the date be fixed April 1932? Was not the local machinery of the Communist Party upset by the arrest of Noulens and Hoiang-Dung-Foh on 14.3.1. The Struggle Settlement reports seem to indicate that there is a Red Central here at present.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.
S. 2, Special Branch
REPORT
Date March 5, 1935.
Subject Letter dated 12.2.35 from the British Consulate-General regarding
organizations associated with the "United Front Campaign."
Made by D. I. Kuh Pao-hwa. Forwarded by [Signature] S.1.

In compliance with the instructions of the D. C.
Special Branch on the attached communication dealing with certain
auxiliary organs of the Comintern, I have to report that
according to information obtained from various sources these
organizations, as far as Shanghai is concerned, exist in name
only. Moreover, organizations possessing titles resembling
those contained in the attached letter have seldom made their
appearance on handbills coming into the possession of the
Municipal Police.

The object of these institutions, as their names
imply, comprises the rendering of assistance to workers and/or
political prisoners as well as the cultivation of friendly
relations with the Soviet Union, and aims at the overthrow of
Imperialism and Fascism.

In consequence of the setback received by the Chinese
Communist Party at the hands of the local Authorities during 1934,
the regular functioning of Comintern organs in this city has
been disrupted. Therefore, the opinion expressed in the attached
letter to the effect that these organs are at present dormant
is perfectly true.

Kuh Pao-hwa
D. I.

D.C. (Special Branch).
S2,
Were the Comintern organs
functioning in 1933 and, if so, where?
D.I. Kuh [Signature] 5/3. [Signature]
5 MAR 1935

SECRET
British Consulate General,
Shanghai,
12th February 1935.

My dear Givens,

I understand on reliable authority that recent
instructions from the Comintern stress the importance which
that organisation attaches to the "United Front Campaign".
The following are the specific organisations
of that front:-
a. Workers International Relief.
b. International Class War Prisoners' Aid.
c. League against Imperialism and for National Independence.
d. Society for Cultural Relations with Soviet Russia.
e. Friends of the Soviet Union.
f. International Union of the Revolutionary Theatre.
g. International Juridical Association.
h. World Committee against War and Fascism.

and I should be grateful for an expression of your view as
to how active in Shanghai any of them may be at the present
moment. My own information leads to the opinion that they
are at present dormant.

Yours sincerely,
[Signature]

T.P.Givens,Esq.,
Special Branch,
S.M.P

D.S. Hokspier.
D.I. Kirk.
D.S. [Unclear]

S2, For comment please
J.H.G
FEB. 12 1935
DMR 4/3

November 29, 1935.

- 2 -

Communist Propaganda - work of Youth Communist
International (Comsomol)

At the sixth world congress of the Youth Communist
International recently convened in Moscow, a resolution
was passed calling for drastic changes in the character of
the work among young communists abroad. While the work
of the Comsomol in the U.S.S.R. is conducted on strictly
communist lines, this organization in foreign countries
is instructed to affiliate with the Socialist Youth,
create a mass youth organization, start a campaign to bring
about world democracy, and overthrow Fascism which is
regarded as the greatest enemy of Communism.

- Activities of the local branch of the Comintern

An examination of communist literature recently
obtained by the Municipal Police indicates that the Chinese
Communist Party is anxious to establish a united front
against Japanese imperialism by arranging co-operation
among all political factions entertaining anti-Government
and anti-Japanese sentiments. In an effort to further the
policy, the communists are trying to resuscitate various
auxiliary organs of the party which discontinued functioning
some months ago as a result of action by the Police of the
various local administrations.
